summary: Hero is not JS-gated: SSR slide 0 is eager/high/opacity 1 and paints without JS (prod HTML no-JS LCP 224 ms); the LH 'fetchpriority=low opacity:0' snippet is a post-autoplay snapshot. Observed FCP->LCP gap 51 ms; the simulated 1.9 s gap is Lantern billing an 826 KB pre-LCP set (prod mobile), 70% JS (575 KB). Lantern what-ifs (fixture h2): today LCP 4.37 s; entry+react-only modulepreload 3.33; entry-only 3.03; no widget/stray chunks 4.22; no JS before LCP (C3) 1.67; C3+hero 640w+one PL font 1.52 (desktop 0.81->0.37). 7 img[fetchpriority=high] + 5 React auto-preloads (4 imagesizes) + wrong builderHeroPreload candidate (DOM-first 25vw card) are latent (+0.9-1.4 s LCP with distinct covers). Consent banner = 27 pp of mobile final-frame histogram, late by 1-2.5 s -> SI -0.55..-0.95 s PSI with SSR shell. Early Hints/speculation ~0 Lantern effect.

findings.claim: The LCP hero is painted from SSR without JS. The production LH snippet (fetchpriority=low, opacity:0) is slide 0 after autoplay moved safeIdx to 1, not its state at paint. The hypothesis 'LCP gated by JS/opacity' is refuted.

findings.claim: Seven img[fetchpriority=high] on '/' (one hero plus six post-list leads in sections 0-2, five below the fold). React 19 auto-preloads every eager img into <head>: 5 image preloads with 4 different imagesizes, plus the app's own preload, plus a Link header. Today this is masked because every widget leads with the same cover URL (mobile: one 768w request). Desktop: 3 High variants (480/768/640w), and the 640w (25 KB) is below the fold. With distinct lead covers it would put 6 extra High images (~150-230 KB) into the pre-LCP set.

findings.claim: builderHeroPreload returns the first preloadable widget in DOM order (a left-column post-list card with 25vw sizes), not the visual LCP (hero slider, 50vw). The explicit head preload and the Link header therefore describe a different candidate than the LCP . On desktop this fetches 480w while the hero needs 768w.

findings.claim: The consent banner is about 27 percentage points of the final mobile frame's histogram completeness and paints 1-2.5 s after content. It cannot be LCP on '/' (paragraph 19 116 px^2 vs hero 68 121 px^2) but can be on pages whose largest element is under ~19 K px^2.

If a tick lands inside the PSI trace, the final frame differs from all earlier frames by the hero (20% mobile / 22% desktop viewport), which inflates observed SI. It did not happen in the M3 run (mobile frames 5420=6504). This is PLAUSIBLE for PSI and unverified without PSI JSON.

findings.claim: Early Hints cannot move Lantern FCP/LCP: requests are hung on the root document node and TTFB/103 are not simulated. Enabling them today would front-load 26 JS modulepreloads from the Link header. Speculation rules are 'moderate', with 0 prefetch/prerender requests in the prod trace. /media can only do WebP (Supabase transforms), so AVIF needs Cloudflare Image Transformations.

changes.title: Single LCP candidate per document: pure lcpCandidate(doc) + context; only its first image is eager+fetchpriority=high, all other images lazy
changes.mechanism: New pure lcpCandidate(doc) next to sectionWidgetsInPaintOrder. It looks at section 0 only and skips abTest and hideOn.desktop. It picks the image widget with the largest desktop slot share; ties go by type rank (slider > image non-logo > dark-featured-card > post-list lead), then DOM order. It depends on the document only, so SSR and the client agree. AboveFoldProvider also carries lcpWidgetId. sliderVariants uses priority={isLcp && i===0} instead of i===0 (lines 1203/1423/1567/1711/1847). PostListView, WidgetView and mediaWidgets use priority={isLcp} instead of aboveFold. The candidate gets data-lcp-candidate. Non-candidates are loading=lazy with fetchpriority auto, so React emits no head preload for them. ABOVE_FOLD_SECTION_COUNT stays 3 for data prefetch only.
changes.expected_effect: Mobile 0 ms today (all leads share one URL). It prevents +0.9..+1.4 s mobile LCP whenever the 6 extra leads carry distinct covers (6 x 25-38 KB High at ~6 ms/KB). Desktop: -25 KB High (640w below the fold) -> <= -0.03 s LCP. Head image preloads 5 -> 1 (plus logo). It is also the precondition for the LP-3/C3 hero signal.
changes.estimate_basis: prod-desktop.json image requests; psi/home.html high-img inventory; lighthouse-analyst Lantern slope 6 ms/KB mobile
changes.risk_notes: Must stay deterministic for SSR/hydration parity, which is why it is a function of the doc, not of query data. Lazy in-viewport cards on desktop load after layout (they are not LCP). Pages whose LCP is a post-list lead (latest_posts mode) still get it because the rule falls back to the post-list lead.
changes.verification: psi-like HTML check: count(img[fetchpriority=high])==1 and count(link[rel=preload][as=image][fetchpriority=high])==1 on / and /en (document-weight gate); LH network list: exactly one High image before LCP on desktop; trace: single largestContentfulPaint::Candidate = data-lcp-candidate; node scripts/performance/lighthouse-local.mjs --compare A B --runs 3 LCP delta >= 0.

changes.title: Preload single source of truth: React auto-preload of the candidate in head; Link header from lcpCandidate; drop builder head imagePreloadLink
changes.mechanism: builderHeroPreload delegates candidate choice to lcpCandidate and builds the descriptor with sliderImageSizes/imageSlotSizes, so it equals the img props. routes/index.tsx:307-312 no longer appends imagePreloadLink for builder docs, because React's highImagePreloads already emits the byte-identical link before the stylesheet. Keep imagePreloadLinkHeaderValue for the Link header (index.tsx:255) as the early-start path and the future Early Hints source. Audit $.tsx and the other routes' head() preload duplicates the same way (keep the Link header, drop the in-head copy when the cover is SSR'd eagerly).
changes.metric: LCP preload correctness (desktop variant), HTML bytes
changes.expected_effect: ≈0 score today. Removes the 25vw->480w mis-preload on desktop and 4 duplicate head links (~7 KB raw / ~1 KB gz). Guarantees that preload == painted candidate for any content.
changes.estimate_basis: prod head inventory; React pushImg semantics
changes.risk_notes: If a future change streams the hero behind Suspense, React would emit its preload late. The Link header still covers that, and the LP-10 gate asserts the head preload exists.
changes.verification: Document-weight gate: the head image preload's imagesrcset+imagesizes equals the data-lcp-candidate img srcset+sizes. The Link header image entry has the same imagesizes.

changes.title: Contract for boot-after-LCP (boot-js C3 / LA-C4): hero signal = img[data-lcp-candidate] load+decode+rAF, else LCP observer / first input / cap; nothing High before it except CSS, one font and the hero
changes.mechanism: The inline bootstrap from C3 waits for document.querySelector('img[data-lcp-candidate]'): complete || load, then img.decode(), then one rAF. Fallbacks: PerformanceObserver largest-contentful-paint first entry, the first pointerdown/keydown/touchstart, or a cap of 1.5-3 s after DOMContentLoaded; if there is no candidate, at DOMContentLoaded+rAF. It must not key on img[fetchpriority=high] (7 today), on slides 2..N, or on fonts. The hero must keep its DOM node through hydration (stable keys), otherwise a re-created img emits a new LCP candidate after JS.
changes.expected_effect: (The C3 effect itself.) Fixture mobile FCP 3973->1367, LCP 4368->1667 (with LP-7/LP-8: 1517); desktop FCP 772->330, LCP 812->410/370. PSI mobile LCP 6.6 -> ~2.0-2.5 s (pre-LCP set 826 -> ~225 KB at ~6 ms/KB).
changes.estimate_basis: whatif.py T0/E6 vs S0 on lha1 artifacts (deterministic); E1/E2 show entry+react-only and entry-only preload policies stay at LCP 3.33/3.03 s
changes.risk_notes: Owned by boot-js C3. The TBT side effect (+0.5..0.8 s on the fixture) requires the LA-C1/hydration program in the same wave. Consent banner and overlays arrive later, which needs LP-4.
changes.verification: Trace: every Script request starts after the observed LCP candidate; single LCP candidate; lighthouse-local --compare FCP/LCP deltas match T0 within 10%.

changes.title: Consent banner SSR shell with pre-paint decided-state script and pre-hydration click intent queue (merge with hydration H9)
changes.mechanism: CONSENT_INIT_SCRIPT is injected after THEME_INIT_SCRIPT (__root.tsx:935). It sets html[data-consent-decided] when consent:v2 (version-checked) or the nes_cookie_consent cookie holds a valid decision. The validity expression is shared as a string fragment from lib/ads/consent.ts, like themeChoice.ts, to avoid copy drift. It also installs one delegated click listener on [data-consent-action] that stores window.__nesConsentIntent. ConsentShell renders static markup (same classes/geometry as the compact card, texts from dehydrated cookie-banner settings + i18n, inline SVG, no lucide/radix) in SSR and on the first client render, only when privacy.cookie_banner && banner.enabled. CSS hides it under html[data-consent-decided]. The lazy ConsentBanner, mounted on idle or immediately when an intent exists, replaces the shell in one commit without animate-in and replays the intent via acceptAll/rejectAll/openPrefs. It remains the only writer of setMarketingConsent/setConsentOverlayVisible.
changes.metric: SI (mobile), LCP stability on text pages, non-composited animation
changes.expected_effect: Mobile SI -0.55..-0.95 s on PSI today (+1.1..+1.6 pts); -0.36 s on the M3 prod run; -0.15 s on the fixture. Prevents a +0.3..0.8 s SI regression after C3. Desktop SI ≈ -0.03 s. On pages where the paragraph would be LCP: LCP ≈ FCP instead of ≥4.8 s. CLS 0.
changes.estimate_basis: Banner = 27.4 pp (mobile) / 4.6 pp (desktop) of histogram progress (prod thumbnails); delay after content 0.95 s (M3) to 1.5-2.5 s (PSI est.); Lantern SI coefficients 1.4/0.4 mobile, 0.575/0.49 desktop; score.py SI curve (4.9 s=0.656, 4.3 s=0.762)

GPC clamp, consent version bump, preview mode and disabled banner must be covered. The shell adds ~2-3 KB raw HTML. Hydration parity: the shell must render identically on the client (no time/locale-dependent text).
gates: SSR/hydration parity tests for root chrome
changes.verification: Filmstrip: the banner is in the first content frame (speedline: no progress jump after FCP); LH mobile SI delta via lighthouse-local --compare (expect -0.1..-0.2 s on fixture); e2e: decided cookie -> shell display:none before first paint (no flash in screenshots at FCP); click on shell before hydration -> consent saved after mount.

changes.title: Slider autoplay gate: start only after first user interaction or whenQuiescent() + in viewport + document visible
changes.mechanism: In SliderRender (:925-941), add a gate state `autoplayArmed`. It is set on the first pointerdown/keydown/touchstart/scroll, or by the TP-4 whenQuiescent() scheduler (after LH-style 5 s quiet), and only while an IntersectionObserver reports the slider visible and document.visibilityState==='visible'. Manual navigation is unchanged. The interval effect depends on autoplayArmed.
changes.expected_effect: Removes the risk of an in-trace slide change (hero 20% of the mobile viewport, 22% desktop). Estimated PSI SI -0..-1.1 s when it would have fired; TBT -0..-60 ms per avoided tick; no Lighthouse-window image fetch for slide 2. 0 on the M3/fixture runs (the tick fell after the trace end / identical fixture images).
changes.estimate_basis: geom hero rects; filmstrip md5 (mobile-04==mobile-05); interval 4500/5500 ms after hydration vs PSI TTI 10.6 s
changes.risk_notes: UX: autoplay begins on first scroll or after quiescence (a few seconds later than today). Respects reduced-motion if added. Verdict PLAUSIBLE: needs PSI JSON (measurement M6) to confirm the in-trace tick.
changes.verification: PSI JSON (M6): the final-screenshot hero equals the first content frame's hero; local LH trace: no setIdx re-render or slide-2 image request before trace end.

changes.mechanism: For isLogo images rendered in header chrome, pass loading=eager (OptimizedImage priority without high, or a new eager prop). React then emits a Low preload and the logo is fetched at parse time instead of after layout. Optimize SVG logos with svgo at upload (26.7 KB raw).

changes.title: CI gate: critical-path invariants in the document-weight check
changes.mechanism: Extend the measurement workstream's gate. On / and /en (fixture artifact), assert: count(img[fetchpriority=high]) <= 1; exactly one head image preload with fetchpriority=high whose imagesrcset/imagesizes equal the data-lcp-candidate img; zero eager images outside the candidate except the logo; Link-header entries limited to an allow-list (after C3: no modulepreload); count(link[rel=modulepreload]) ratchet.
changes.expected_effect: No direct delta. It stops the 7-high/5-preload pattern and stray JS hints from returning.
changes.risk_notes: Thresholds must start at the post-LP-1 values and ratchet.
changes.verification: The gate fails on the baseline artifact (7 high imgs) and passes after LP-1/LP-2.

changes.title: Link header policy = CSS + one font + LCP image only; Cloudflare Early Hints only after that (human decision)
changes.mechanism: Remove modulepreload, widget and stray entries and the supabase preconnect from the Link header for anonymous documents (after C3 nothing JS-side is needed before LCP). Then enable Early Hints in the Cloudflare zone and verify that 103 carries only those 3-4 hints.
changes.expected_effect: 0 Lighthouse points (Lantern hangs requests on the document node and does not simulate TTFB/103). Real users on MISS start CSS/font/hero ~server time earlier. It prevents EH from front-loading ~575 KB of JS.
changes.estimate_basis: Lantern graph semantics; psi/h1.txt (31 Link entries)
changes.risk_notes: Workers + edge document cache + EH compatibility is unverified here (no egress). Speculation rules need no change (moderate, 0 in-trace prefetches).
changes.verification: curl -sI on production shows a Link header with <=4 entries; (human) 103 visible in Chrome netlog.

changes.title: AVIF for /media via Cloudflare Image Transformations (cf.image format=auto) — human/cost decision
changes.mechanism: In media.$.ts, for transformable paths, fetch with cf.image {width, quality, format: Accept-negotiated avif|webp} instead of the Supabase render endpoint. Keep Vary: Accept and immutable caching.
changes.expected_effect: Hero ≈ -30%: mobile LCP -0.15 s today, 0 after C3; desktop -0.02..-0.04 s.
changes.risk_notes: Paid transformation quota. Decode cost of AVIF on low-end devices. Two transform pipelines.
changes.verification: LH hero request content-type image/avif and transfer size; lighthouse-local --compare.
